html:
SMTO-SKL-0087 — Your email may or may not have been sent

GUID: 319a4102-491c-5719-b497-6e4c85e3def6
Slug: microsoft365-mail-send-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO asked Microsoft to send your email, but the reply was lost. The email may already be on its way, so SMTO won't send it again on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: open Outlook with the same Microsoft account and look in Sent Items for the email by recipient and subject. Microsoft may have sent it even though SMTO never got the confirmation.
  2. If you were sending a saved draft, also check whether it's still in your Drafts folder. A draft that has left Drafts was most likely sent.
  3. Wait a few minutes and look again; if it still isn't in Sent Items, ask SMTO to send it again and approve the send. Sending twice without checking could give the recipient two copies.

What success looks like

  • The email appears once in your Sent Items.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the recipient and time, to the person who manages SMTO. If you're unsure, ask the recipient whether it arrived instead of resending.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 mail_send, mail_send_draft, mail_reply, mail_reply_all or mail_forward request lost reliable acknowledgement after it was sent (network failure, 500/502/503/504, unexpected success status or unreadable response), so the result is mail_send_outcome_unknown.

What this means

  • A send, send-draft, reply, reply-all or forward request loses reliable mutation acknowledgement and uses the mail_send outcome-unknown family. Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.

Why this can happen

  • A send, send-draft, reply, reply-all or forward request loses reliable mutation acknowledgement and uses the mail_send outcome-unknown family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact draft/message, Sent Items and provider request evidence; delivery cannot be proved by a missing acknowledgement.

How to fix it

  • Check whether your action already happened: look in Sent Items (and, for mail_send_draft, whether the draft left Drafts) under the same account_ref with microsoft365.mail_search, matching recipients, subject and time. Do not resend while the original send remains uncertain; send a new message only after confirming it is absent.
  • Inspect the exact message and Sent Items using retained request evidence; do not resend while the original send remains uncertain.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Send state is reconciled without automatically resending the message.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
